evals.prompt: Loan applications should only move to `approved` if the applicant's credit score from our bureau API is above 700, and the caller should see why when it's refused. We write Python.
evals.expected_output: Decides a function criterion is needed (data not on the entity, and a user-visible reason). Fetches field names from cyoda help cloudevents json (processing/EntityCriteriaCalculationRequest/Response) and stubs from cyoda help grpc proto. Explains join (the node's own M2M client's client_credentials token, joinedLegalEntityId, greet first, ack), keep-alive per grpc KEEPALIVE, tag routing per grpc TAG ROUTING. The handler returns matches on every answer that isn't an explicit success: false and, on false, a reason (Cyoda keeps the first 2048 characters) that appears in the 400 WORKFLOW_FAILED detail for a manual transition and in TRANSITION_NOT_MATCH_CRITERION audit data.reason for automated ones. Python code uses the schema names, not invented ones. It may name `cyoda:build` as covering wiring the criterion into the workflow. No typed command.

assertions.text: Fetches `cyoda help cloudevents json` (EntityCriteriaCalculationResponse) and/or `cyoda help grpc proto` before writing code, and names grpc sections (COMPUTE MEMBER PROTOCOL, TAG ROUTING or KEEPALIVE)
Chooses a function criterion (not a processor, not an inline criterion), because the data isn't on the entity
Returns `matches: false` with a `reason` when refused
Every answer that isn't a failure carries `matches`, and a failure to evaluate is reported with an explicit `success: false` (not an `error` object alone)
Says where the reason shows up: the 400 WORKFLOW_FAILED detail for a manual transition and/or the TRANSITION_NOT_MATCH_CRITERION audit event's data.reason

Covers the join: a token of the node's own M2M client from `client_credentials` (not an on-behalf-of or `cyoda token` token), CalculationMemberJoinEvent with tags and joinedLegalEntityId, greet first, acknowledge
Continues without asking the developer to type a command: no 'type `/cyoda:…`' or 'next, type …', neither in its own words nor in a warning it relays

evals.prompt: Our processor config has calculationNodesTags "billing,eu,priority". A colleague says the node must declare all required tags. Do I really have to register all three on every node?
evals.expected_output: Reads grpc --section "TAG ROUTING" (workflows PROCESSORS agrees): one overlapping tag is enough; round robin among matching members; empty tags match any member of the tenant. Advises a tag of its own for a member that must receive a callout, and identical spelling on both sides.

assertions.text: Reads `cyoda-help.sh grpc --section "TAG ROUTING"` and bases the answer on it
Says one shared tag is enough; registering all three is not required
Does not claim that cyoda help contradicts itself on tag matching and does not cite #684 item B
Says several matching members are picked round robin, so a member that must receive a callout needs a tag of its own
Does not say the node's tags must be a superset of the processor's tags

evals.prompt: My processor calls a document-signing service that takes 40-50 seconds. It keeps failing. What should I change?
evals.expected_output: Reads workflows PROCESSORS and grpc KEEPALIVE / config grpc. The response timeout is responseTimeoutMs; unset or 0 is the server's CYODA_CALLOUT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS (30 s by default), so 40-50 s fails with DISPATCH_TIMEOUT, and import refuses a value above CYODA_CALLOUT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS (60 s by default). Recommends COMMIT_BEFORE_DISPATCH with a raised responseTimeoutMs and an idempotent processor (a replay dispatches it again; the pre-callout state is visible), with `idempotent: true` declared only if a repeat of the signing call is harmless (with it, a processor that got no answer goes to another compute member; without it, the callout fails), and keeping the stream answered (acks/keep-alive) within CYODA_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT (default 30 s) while the call runs. It may name `cyoda:build` as covering the workflow change. No typed command.

assertions.text: Reads `workflows --section PROCESSORS` and `grpc --section KEEPALIVE` (or `cyoda help config grpc`) for the timeout and keep-alive values
Says the default response timeout is 30 s when responseTimeoutMs is unset or 0 (the server's CYODA_CALLOUT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_MS)
Does not state a 60-second default response timeout or keep-alive (60 s as the upper bound on responseTimeoutMs is fine)
Recommends COMMIT_BEFORE_DISPATCH (or an execution mode from workflows PROCESSORS) with a raised responseTimeoutMs

Says the processor must be idempotent because a replay dispatches it again, and recommends declaring `idempotent: true` only if a repeat of the signing call is harmless everywhere (it lets Cyoda give a processor that got no answer to another compute member)
Says the node must keep acknowledging/answering within CYODA_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT while the slow call runs
Continues without asking the developer to type a command: no 'type `/cyoda:…`' or 'next, type …', neither in its own words nor in a warning it relays

evals.prompt: When an Order is paid, its Shipment (we keep shipmentId on the order) should move to `ready`, in the same transaction. How does my processor do that?
evals.expected_output: A processor on the order's pay transition fires a manual transition on the linked Shipment by id: PATCH /api/entity/JSON/{shipmentId}/{transition} with merge-patch, If-Match: * and {} (crud ENDPOINTS). To be in the same transaction, echo the cyodatxtoken CloudEvent extension as X-Tx-Token (HTTP) or tx-token (gRPC metadata) per cluster COMPUTE CALLBACK TRANSACTION ROUTING; which modes provide a usable transaction is in workflows PROCESSORS. The shipment transition is manual: true. Doesn't write the order itself through a callback; changes it only through returned data. Language-agnostic pseudocode.

assertions.text: Names `workflows --section PROCESSORS` and the transaction-token source (`cluster` COMPUTE CALLBACK TRANSACTION ROUTING) and/or `crud --section ENDPOINTS`
The processor fires a manual transition on the linked Shipment by its id with PATCH `{}` (merge-patch, If-Match), not by editing the shipment's state field
Echoes the `cyodatxtoken` extension as `X-Tx-Token` or `tx-token` so the call joins the originating transaction, and says that without it the call commits separately
Says the shipment's transition should be `manual: true`
Gives the pattern without assuming a language the developer didn't name

evals.prompt: Do I need a compute node to approve invoices automatically when the amount is under 1000?
evals.expected_output: No: an inline simple criterion ($.amount LESS_THAN 1000) on an automated transition does it (workflows CRITERIA / search CONDITION DSL). A compute node is needed only for data not on the entity, external calls, a user-visible rejection reason, or a per-entity schedule time. It may name `cyoda:build` as covering adding the criterion. No typed command.

assertions.text: Names `workflows --section CRITERIA` (or `search --section "CONDITION DSL"`) for the criterion
Says no compute node is needed and proposes an inline simple criterion on an automated transition
Says when a compute node would be needed (other data, an external call, a rejection reason, or a computed schedule)
Continues without asking the developer to type a command: no 'type `/cyoda:…`' or 'next, type …', neither in its own words nor in a warning it relays
